The original film, the original wvent, an original photo (There were several)? It does establish later in the report that it is a Polaroid of an original photo, but this sentence's lack of completion really threw me off.

Still, this is a well rounded report and interview, +1.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Well, I liked it. And I liked the interview too. It was an interview being conducted with a man who, while under the effects of an SCP object that produces auditory and visual hallucinations, was confronted with a potentially violent situation. He attempted to resolve the situation rationally without blowing cover; that's what the money was there for, not every recovery is "eight dudes in paramilitary gear roll up in a van, smash-and-grab, then amnesiac everyone and leave."

The potentially violent situation turned violent, and the old guy *caught on fire himself*. Now did the guy ACTUALLY catch fire, or was it an effect of the photo? Could be either one… Until we get to the bit about the house burning down, centered on the old man's corpse.

Was the old man affected by the photo too? Was he something else that (accidentally?) gave the photo its anomalies? Are there more like him out there? That's the type of titillation that earns an upvote from me.
